title: I Think I have it
author: Alone_Tart_3775
selftext:
A better definition of AGE.

AGE is a **linguistic game engine** that takes pure language, interprets it as systemic logic, and produces structured, deterministic game systems.  
It outputs complete pre‑production documentation and defines mechanics, rules, and world logic.  
AGE imposes **no genre**, **no identity**, **no narrative**, and **no setting** — the developer decides everything. And yes, I used AI to help me draft this post. as there has been some speculation about what I am building and the above is the plainest way I could think of to put it. So thanks for the read 

arron

replies.author: Alone_Tart_3775
replies.body:
You’re mixing two different things:

**1. Natural language as people casually use it** — yes, that’s often non‑deterministic.  
**2. Constrained language used as code** — that’s deterministic by design.

BASIC wasn’t about being “modern,” it was about proving that plain words, when constrained, can drive deterministic behavior. The same is true of modern languages: they’re closer to natural language *in syntax*, but they’re still rule‑bound, fixed‑state systems.

AGE works on the same principle: constrained language, strict rules, no inference. I’m not claiming “all language is deterministic,” I’m saying **structured language can be used deterministically**—and that’s exactly what I’ve built AGE around.
